title: API 580 Training in Midland, TX: RBI Exam Prep Online
description: Self-paced API 580 risk based inspection exam prep for Permian gas plant and terminal RBI teams, inspection planners and integrity engineers. Instructor Q&A.
h1: API 580 Training in Midland: Risk-Based Inspection Exam Prep for Permian Gas Plant and Terminal Teams
html:
API 580 exam prep for RBI work in the Permian Basin

Risk-based inspection has followed the growth of Permian processing. A single gas processing company can now run several near-identical plants across the Midland Basin, and inspecting every vessel and circuit on a fixed calendar spreads effort evenly over equipment that is not evenly at risk. RBI is how an owner points that effort at the items whose probability and consequence of failure justify it. This page is for the engineers, planners and inspectors who build and maintain those programmes around Midland and are preparing for the API 580 examination.

There is no Atlantis classroom in Midland. The API 580 course is self-paced and online, with instructor Q&A: you study when your work allows and send questions as they come up. The American Petroleum Institute decides eligibility, administers the API 580 examination and issues the certification. Atlantis is not an API-approved provider, and the course does not award the credential.

Who sits API 580 in Midland

RBI teams around Midland draw on a mix of people, and API's eligibility rules accommodate most of them. Holders of a current API 510, API 570 or API 653 certification qualify automatically, the usual route for plant and contract inspectors. Engineers and planners without an inspector certification qualify through education plus petrochemical industry experience gained in the last ten years, from one year with a bachelor's degree to five or more with no formal education. Typical candidates include:

  • Mechanical integrity engineers at gas processing and NGL companies, who own the RBI model and defend it in audits.
  • Inspection planners who turn risk rankings into work orders, outage scopes and CML schedules.
  • Corrosion and materials specialists who assign damage mechanisms and rates to each corrosion loop.
  • Terminal integrity staff who manage tank and station piping programmes at the Midland and Crane hubs.
  • Operations and reliability leads who sit on the team because they know how the plant actually runs.

Whether years in gas processing count as petrochemical industry experience is for API to judge from your application, so describe the plant, the work and your role precisely. The API 580 course page covers the exam and the study approach in full.

Where RBI is required, where it is chosen, and where it is rarely used

No rule around Midland demands RBI by name, but the rules decide where a formal mechanical integrity programme exists for RBI to sit in.

  • Gas plants are covered by OSHA's process safety management standard. OSHA has said so plainly, citing the preamble it published with the standard in 1992. PSM's mechanical integrity element requires inspection and testing that follow recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices, at frequencies consistent with manufacturers' recommendations and good practice, and more often if operating experience calls for it. API 510 and API 570 both let an RBI assessment set inspection intervals, which is how RBI enters a gas plant's PSM programme.
  • Production facilities have been treated differently. In a 2005 interpretation letter OSHA described a policy of not enforcing PSM at oil and gas production facilities pending an economic feasibility analysis, and the standard exempts normally unoccupied remote facilities. Out on the leases, RBI is usually an owner's planning choice rather than part of a PSM programme.
  • EPA's risk management rule counts from the plant inlet. Under 40 CFR 68.115, naturally occurring hydrocarbon mixtures, meaning field gas, condensate, crude oil and produced water, need not be counted toward threshold quantities before they enter a natural gas processing plant. The fence line is where RMP coverage can begin.

The result is a sharp line at the fence. Inside a gas plant, an RBI model is part of a regulated integrity programme and has to be documented, kept current and defended. On gathering systems and leases, the same method can be used as a planning tool with far less formality. The exam is written around RP 580, which describes a complete programme, so a Midland candidate should learn its documentation and reassessment expectations in full even if the equipment they manage sits outside PSM. The comparison of RMP and PSM mechanical integrity sets the two rules side by side.

A gas plant RBI model, loop by loop

RP 580 asks for damage mechanisms to be identified before probability is assessed, and a cryogenic gas plant divides naturally into corrosion loops with very different stories:

LoopTypical damage to assessMain consequence drivers
Inlet separation and compressionCarbon dioxide and wet H2S corrosion, erosion at inlets, vibration fatigue on small-bore connectionsFlammable gas at high pressure, often with H2S
Amine treatingAmine corrosion, amine stress corrosion cracking, wet H2S cracking on the rich sideAcid gas and toxic H2S release
DehydrationThermal cycling on molecular sieve vessels, corrosion from degraded glycolFlammable gas
Cryogenic recoveryLittle internal corrosion, but brittle fracture and low-temperature excursionsLarge flammable inventory that vaporises rapidly
NGL product and storageExternal corrosion, CUI on cold lines, auto-refrigeration on releaseLight hydrocarbons and vapour cloud potential

Two features set Permian models apart from refinery ones. Consequence can vary sharply between plants: a site in open country and a site within reach of a town or a highway do not carry the same consequence to people, and Statewide Rule 36, the Railroad Commission's hydrogen sulfide rule, already requires operators to calculate a radius of exposure for H2S from gas composition and escape rate. That calculation is a ready input to the toxic side of a consequence model. And many plants are new. A train started in the last few years has baseline readings and design data but no corrosion history, so its first assessment leans on predicted rates and has to be revisited once real inspection data arrive.

Fleets of near-identical plants

Midland Basin processing has grown by repeating designs. Most of Targa's recent plants are rated at 275 million cubic feet a day, Enterprise's Midland Basin plants such as Leonidas and Athena at around 300 million, and Energy Transfer took on eight operating plants when it bought WTG Midstream in 2024. A company with several similar trains is tempted to build one RBI model and copy it. A sister plant's corrosion data can reasonably inform a first assessment, but only where feed gas, operating conditions and materials genuinely match, and the assumption has to be written down and tested as the plant's own data come in. Expect exam questions on data quality, assumptions and what triggers a reassessment; a fleet model is a good place to practise answering them.

Terminals and breakout tanks: where RBI meets a federal limit

Much of the crude storage at Midland and Crane belongs to pipeline terminals; ONEOK's Longhorn pipeline, for one, has origin points at Crane, Barnhart and Midland. Where an atmospheric or low-pressure steel tank is a breakout tank under 49 CFR Part 195, section 195.432 requires its physical integrity to be inspected to API 653 but does not allow API 653's risk-based method to set its internal inspection interval. PHMSA published a proposal in June 2026 that would allow RBI under the fifth edition of API 653 for breakout tanks, capped at 20 years for the first internal inspection and 25 years for later ones. It was a proposal, not a final rule, when this page was written. Tanks that are not breakout tanks, at a gas plant or a refinery, sit outside that federal restriction.

For a terminal RBI team, that leaves the station piping, pumps and non-breakout tankage as the equipment where risk can set intervals today, with breakout tank internals on the standard API 653 rules for now. The storage tank RBI page explains how tank RBI is structured.

A closed-book scenario: which change lowers the risk?

The API 580 exam is closed-book and conceptual, so it rewards clear thinking about what each action does to probability and to consequence. Try this on an amine contactor at a Midland Basin plant. The RBI team has ranked it high because wet H2S cracking is credible and the inspection history is thin. Which of these changes reduces the assessed risk, and how?

  1. A more effective inspection, such as an angle-beam or phased array ultrasonic examination of the welds for cracking. It does not change the damage, but it reduces uncertainty about the damage state, so the assessed probability of failure falls.
  2. Adding gas detection and faster isolation. This leaves probability alone and lowers consequence, by limiting how much gas escapes and how far it travels.
  3. Repeating the same thickness survey more often. This adds little, because a thickness survey is not an effective technique for the cracking that drives the ranking.
  4. Changing the amine or its loading. A process change can lower the probability of the mechanism itself, which is why management of change and integrity operating windows belong inside an RBI programme.

The reasoning is what the exam is after: inspection lowers risk only by reducing uncertainty, and an inspection that cannot find the expected damage buys almost nothing.

Studying for API 580 next to a full-time integrity job

The paper has 90 questions, 80 of them scored, in 3.25 hours with no books, and it is built on API RP 580 rather than a set of codes. That makes it a reading and understanding exam. A self-paced approach suits it well: read RP 580 a section at a time, restate the terms in your own words, and test yourself on why each element of an RBI programme exists, not just what it is called. The instructor answers questions where RP 580 language and the language of your plant's RBI software do not line up, a common stumbling point for people who use a tool every day. Check API's delivery options for your window when you apply, since the programme page describes both test centre and remote proctored sittings.

Exam preparation and an RBI study are different jobs

Preparing for API 580 does not produce an RBI assessment for any plant, and the course neither uses nor replaces an owner's RBI software. Where an owner needs the assessment itself, Atlantis carries out remote RBI studies as a separate engagement, working from the owner's data, and the owner's inspector of record approves the resulting intervals. Keeping the two apart matters for clarity and for independence.

Sponsoring API 580 candidates from a Midland site

A sponsored group works best when it includes the people who will maintain the model, not only those who built it. Employers can enrol planners, engineers and inspectors together on one quote, and fees are quoted on request. Give each candidate one loop of the plant's own model to explain against RP 580 as they study; it is the quickest way to find out whether the model's assumptions are written down.

faq.q: Is there an API 580 course in Midland?
faq.a: There is no Atlantis classroom in Midland. The API 580 course is self-paced online with instructor Q&A, so planners and engineers can study around outages and audits without travelling. API runs the examination and issues the certification. Its programme page describes test centre and remote proctored sittings, so confirm the options for your window when you apply.

faq.q: Must a Midland planner hold an inspector certification before sitting API 580?
faq.a: No, although holding one helps. A current API 510, API 570 or API 653 certification qualifies you automatically. Without one, API looks at education plus petrochemical industry experience from the last ten years, from one year with a bachelor's degree to five or more with no formal education. API verifies what you put on the application.

faq.q: Does gas processing experience count for API 580?
faq.a: API makes that call from your application, so describe the plant and your role accurately: the units, the RBI or inspection work you did, and your employer. Gas plants handle many of the same mechanisms, equipment types and process safety obligations as refining and chemical sites, but API, not the course provider or your employer, decides whether your experience meets the requirement.

faq.q: Is API 580 required to run RBI at a Texas gas plant?
faq.a: No regulation we have found names API 580 as a requirement. OSHA's PSM standard, which covers gas plants, requires inspection and testing that follow recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices, and API 510 and API 570 allow RBI to set intervals within that framework. Owners decide who leads their RBI work, and many look for API 580 as evidence of knowledge.

faq.q: Can RBI set the internal interval on a breakout tank at Crane?
faq.a: Not under 49 CFR 195.432 as written when this page was published: the rule requires atmospheric steel breakout tanks to be inspected to API 653 but bars API 653's risk-based method from setting the internal interval. PHMSA proposed in June 2026 to allow it under the fifth edition of API 653, with caps of 20 and 25 years. Check whether that proposal has become a final rule.

faq.q: Will the course teach our plant's RBI software?
faq.a: No. The course prepares you for the API 580 examination, which tests RP 580 concepts rather than any software. Vendors train their own tools. What the course does help with is translating software outputs back into RP 580 terms, so you can explain a ranking to an auditor or a turnaround planner and recognise when a default value is driving the answer.

faq.q: Are there calculations on the API 580 exam?
faq.a: Very few. The Body of Knowledge has no calculation section of the kind the API 510, 570 and 653 papers carry, and the questions test understanding and vocabulary: probability and consequence, risk ranking, inspection effectiveness, data, the team and reassessment. Expect to read a risk matrix and reason about it rather than run numbers.

faq.q: How long does API 580 certification last?
faq.a: Three years. API accepts recertification applications from 90 days before the expiry date and allows a 90-day grace period after it. API has said employment verification is not currently required to recertify API 580, but check the current rules on API's site when your renewal comes round, as programme requirements can change.
